video_title: Cavs or Knicks? RJ & Channing Go ALL IN On Their ECF Picks

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on Ausar Thompson's offensive struggles
quotes.excerpt: He got to give them something more than five points. With his God-given athletic ability, the kid could be an All-Star.
quotes.quote: I didn't say anything mean about Ausar Thompson. To everyone listening, I didn't say anything mean about Ausar Thompson. His name is Ausar. I'm just kidding. Ausar, right? Listen, is he an absolute demon defensively? For sure. That's actually where the conversation started. It's where it started. Guys, come on. You can't watch the game and not say, yeah, I got a little, I got a little animated about it, but only because I think one, the Pistons need another scorer. And if he's going to play 48 minutes a night, he got to give them something more than five points. With his God-given athletic ability, the kid could be an All-Star every single year if he just had a jumper. And that was my whole point.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on Ausar Thompson's diverse scoring development
quotes.excerpt: It's not just a jumper, it's learning how to play basketball and put yourself in a good offensive position.
quotes.quote: It's not just a jumper. I'll back you up on this. It's not just a jumper because there's a lot of guys that learn to score in ways that aren't just shooting a spot-up three or pull-up. It means more in transition. It means more downhill. It means learning when to cut back cut, being in the dunker spot, learning how to do a hand-off, a fake hand-off and going because they mess up the switch. Like, you don't have, you can put hundreds of hours in on a jumper and that will improve over time. But also learning how to play basketball and put yourself in a good offensive position, right? It's not just shoot a jumper, it's putting yourself in a good offensive position to contribute more offensively than what he is.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye on the Thompson twins' defensive prowess and offensive need
quotes.excerpt: If Wemby didn't exist, they would go for Defensive Player of the Year, they'd be up there every single year.
quotes.quote: Here's the greatest compliment. Between him and his brother, if Wemby didn't exist, they would go for Defensive Player of the Year, they'd be up there every single year. As defensive, if Wemby did not exist, right? So for me, it's just like, and then you look at these games and you're like, dog, you're avoiding that whole side of the basketball court. And I'm just like, man, for them to be great, that I mean, obviously, Duren needs to work on it too. They just need to really, they have established themselves defensively sometimes, not last night. But man, for that team to take the real step, those guys got to really focus in this summer, and they're young, I think they're 23, 22, on being, being more of a threat on that end of the floor because it's not fun to watch them just, they just look at Cade and they're like, alright, score some points for us and if we get a layup, we get a layup.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye praises Cleveland's team play and bigs' engagement
quotes.excerpt: Donovan Mitchell was efficient. Evan Mobley, Jarrett Allen, and the others were dialed, absolutely dialed in.
quotes.quote: Donovan Mitchell was efficient. Evan Mobley, Jarrett Allen, and the others were dialed, absolutely dialed in. I think one thing that Jarrett Allen said after the game was he was giving Donovan a lot of credit. He said, hey, he wasn't necessarily going to have this 40, 50 point night, but he also didn't force the issue offensively, which allowed us to get into a rhythm together. And so, you know, I have said, hey, there are certain times and certain games where your best scorer has to become a playmaker, where he's drawing two, getting the other guys involved. You look at Sam Merrill, you look at what Strus has done. You look at Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, I don't know if those guys each series they have become, each game, more and more engaged on both ends of the floor. Evan Mobley, hello! Right? It's good basketball to watch. It is good basketball to watch. And guess what? James Harden, you don't need him to get you 20. You don't need him to have the ball in his hands like that, like the other some of the other games. You just need him to just be that guy that's just going to feed everybody.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on the pressure on Cavs and Knicks, and Pistons' offensive issues
quotes.excerpt: The Pistons had an incomplete offense. Their offense just wasn't, they didn't have enough scorers.
quotes.quote: Cleveland and the Knicks. Why was there so much pressure on Cleveland and the Knicks this year? One, Boston, they were supposed to be down Jason Tatum. No one believed in Philly. Orlando didn't take a step up. Detroit looked like an incomplete basketball team even though we're they were great. People didn't start falling in love with Boston till the end of the season when they saw how healthy they were with Jason Tatum, right? That's when people started falling in love with Boston. I say all this to say, the Pistons had an incomplete offense. Their offense just wasn't, they didn't have enough scorers just in general on top of having a guy that played a ton of minutes, be on the court like all the time and not really contribute offensively. So that's why people looked at the Knicks and Cleveland like, hey, if these two teams don't do it this year, next year is not going to get easier. So when I look at Detroit and how their season ended, it ended how we somewhat expected that offensively they weren't going to have enough firepower in the playoffs. With Cleveland, the thing that we questioned was their toughness, could they be consistent, could they be late game when they needed? And they were. They did it. It was impressive. Shout out Cleveland, but they also did it again and in a they did it against a team that was great all year long, but they had an advantage. If they could maintain enough offensive firepower against Detroit's defense, then they were going to get through and that's what they did, they proved that they can do that.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: Allie Clifton and Richard Jefferson discuss the Knicks' rest advantage
quotes.excerpt: The Knicks last played May 10th, which means they will have had nine days of rest before Tuesday's Game 1.

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: The Knicks last played May 10th, which means they will have had nine days of rest before Tuesday's Game 1. You two are superstars when it comes to that. Real talk though, it is kind of like there's some trickery to it. There is some trickery to it. You have to make sure that you are not...

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Oh, that's great. I love that. Give me that. Give me nine days. No, you have to go so hard in practice conditioning-wise, and you're still going to have some jitters, you're still going to have this, but the only thing you got to consider is making sure your conditioning doesn't drop.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson on intense conditioning to maintain fitness during breaks
quotes.excerpt: We would all line up and there were six VersaClimers... and we would do first quarter VersaClimer five minutes.
quotes.quote: No, you have to go so hard in practice conditioning-wise, and you're still going to have some jitters, you're still going to have this, but the only thing you got to consider is making sure your conditioning doesn't drop. And that means doing VersaClimer. We would, we would all line up and there were six VersaClimers and it was like groups and we would do first quarter VersaClimer five minutes. Then the next group would go. Yeah, it was like five of them in a row. And then we would do it. Then we would go second quarter and we'd have to hit a number. And it was all of us in a row doing this on the VersaClimer. So we're one not pounding on our bodies, knees, backs, all that stuff. Our VersaClimers are the worst. Dante Jones, shout out our guy Dante. Dante Jones, he joined the VersaClimer, he joined the group, right, right before the postseason. So he was in NBA conditioning. He wasn't in great conditioning, but he's in NBA conditioning. He showed up and almost died doing the VersaClimer because we would go so hard.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: Allie Clifton and Richard Jefferson discuss OG Anunoby's rest benefit
quotes.excerpt: If there was something great that came out of the nine days off, OG Anunoby.

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: When you needed him in what, Game 6? Was it Game 6, Game 4?

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Yeah, Game 6, he showed up. He got an and-one, he got like a stop, an offensive foul, hit another bucket. And it was like foul trouble that we were dealing with a bunch of different things. And then maybe the Warriors had cut it to like 10 or something, eight. They cut it to a manageable number and he had back-to-back plays that gave us that little boost going into the second half.

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: He made the point about if there was a something great that came out of the nine days off, OG Anunoby. Obviously, he's been recovering from a right hamstring strain that kept him out of Games 3 and 4 of the second round.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: Allie Clifton and Richard Jefferson debate the impact of rest versus fatigue
quotes.excerpt: Does this hurt or help the Knicks? Does the seven-game semifinals hurt or help the Cavs?

text_blocks.speaker: Allie Clifton
text_blocks.text: The Knicks would have had to start on the road if it was the Pistons, but now home court advantage since it's the Cavs playing the first two games at MSG with the Cavs coming off a tiring series. Obviously, you think maybe it has an impact? Does this hurt or help the Knicks? Does the seven-game semifinals hurt or help the Cavs? I think it could help them from a rhythm standpoint is what I'm saying. Obviously, you're exhausted, but at this point, who isn't exhausted?

text_blocks.speaker: Richard Jefferson
text_blocks.text: Nah. Give me the rested team.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson explains why rest is a significant advantage for the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: The rest for the Knicks, especially because they had people banged up, they're playing at a fast pace, they needed a break.
quotes.quote: The rest for the Knicks, especially because they had people banged up, they're playing at a fast pace, they needed a break. And you see it. You can say that about Cleveland. Cleveland had to battle against Toronto. They had to battle against. That stuff adds up. You don't think so, but when that other team has been resting, making sure their bodies go from from 88% up to 93% health because they're able to rest and relax, meanwhile, your health on your team is dwindling. You know, your little power button when you're playing in FIFA, your turbo button is draining, right? And theirs is gaining. And so from that standpoint, give me the rested team. There is an edge. Those first game or two are important because you don't want to have to exert extra energy to try and like even it up. I'll take the Knicks.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye details the Knicks' strategic advantage from extended rest
quotes.excerpt: You've given the New York Knicks nine extra days to study you, to game plan you.
quotes.quote: You know what we're not even taking into account? Both of those teams are shooting out all their different game plans. So like Max Strus starting, Dean Wade starting. Like they're going into their, they're going deep into the bag to win these games as the opponent is watching them. So you've given the New York Knicks nine extra days to study you, to game plan you. And there's only, there's only so much, right, that you can do with your team, right, that they haven't seen before. So, you know, Kenny Atkinson may be like, damn, what can I, what can we do to win this series? While Mike Brown's going, oh, if he does this, we have this. If he does that, we have this. He's looking at substitution patterns. He's looking at how many minutes guys play. So now the Knicks are focusing and locking in on the Cavs or whoever was going to win, while the Cavs and Detroit are just punching each other in the face. So the Knicks, man, I'm going with the Knicks rested. Yeah, it's pretty crazy.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson praises Ian Eagle as a mentor and the funniest person
quotes.excerpt: Ian Eagle is the first guy when I was fresh out of retirement, the first game I ever called was with Ian Eagle.
quotes.quote: So Ian Eagle is the first guy when I was fresh out of retirement, the first game I ever called was with Ian Eagle and the Nets. And so he's been a mentor, he's a legend. The funniest person, the funniest human being I've ever been around my entire life. Like he is so good, so legit. And like I hear calls all the time. I, I, I forgot what, I stole one of his for an ESPN broadcast. I was like, he hit him with the fro fake with Jarrett Allen, like Jarrett Allen did like a fake, like a fake one way. I texted him. I was like, yo, I think I used your your fro fake or one of his jokes on a thing. He's like, what's mine is yours, Rich. I'm like, salute, salute my guy Ian.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye identifies Mitchell Robinson as the X-factor and highlights Cavs' bigs' redemption
quotes.excerpt: I think the best player obviously is Jalen Brunson, then Donovan, then KAT, then Evan Mobley, then OG, then James Harden.
quotes.quote: I'm going to say Mitchell Robinson. In the whole series. Here's why. Here's why. I think the best player obviously is Jalen Brunson, then Donovan, then KAT, then Evan Mobley, then OG, then James Harden, right? I think that if Mitchell Robinson can make an impact offensive rebounding, defensively, because one thing I love about this series is this should be very, very, very personal for the Cleveland bigs. They are three years older, they're three years stronger, they've shown that they are not soft. They've had two crazy tough series. Now they have to beat the team that basically made them look soft. I think back in the day, three years ago, two years ago, whatever it was, they got bullied. They got bullied. So there ain't no more bullying. Ain't no more bullying now when it comes to to the Cavs and the Knicks. And so if Mitchell Robinson can offensive rebound, defense, do stuff like that, then I think he's going to be a huge X-factor and then they can't attack the paint.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson highlights Karl-Anthony Towns' playmaking as a key offensive X-factor
quotes.excerpt: Karl-Anthony Towns and his playmaking and them putting the ball in his hands has really upped their offense.
quotes.quote: I would say X-factor, I would go bigs also. And again, because Karl-Anthony Towns and his playmaking and them putting the ball in his hands has really upped their offense because now guys are getting easy buckets, OG's getting an easy bucket here, Mikal Bridges, they're messing up switches. So him and his assists, multiple triple-doubles in this postseason. So that, but what happens is is you put a small on him, you put a small on him, he's big. Like you put a small to pressure him, he can see over, he can see over that. You put a big on him and he can drive by the big. He can drive by the big, there's no problem because bigs aren't used to pressure him. Joel Embiid wasn't going to get up and pressure him. Drummond wasn't going to get up and pressure him. So he could basically pick him apart. Now you flip it. Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen are the prototypical bigs that you want to guard him. They can pressure him and they have the feet and the mobility to guard him if he goes on the move. So I think that the bigs, how well Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen guard Karl-Anthony Towns because now he's the hub of the offense.

quotes.speaker: Allie Clifton
quotes.summary_phrase: Allie Clifton and Richard Jefferson discuss Ian Eagle's 'Spida-bite' call

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson ranks top players and identifies key matchups for the series
quotes.excerpt: I still think if you talk about an individual talent basis, the best player in the series is probably Donovan Mitchell.
quotes.quote: I still think if you talk about an individual talent basis, the best player in the series is probably Donovan Mitchell. In the last three years, Jalen Brunson has proven to be one of the best guards, if not the best guard in the conference. I'm probably going to lean with Jalen Brunson because this is his second go-around in a Conference Finals, and this is Donovan Mitchell's first time playing this far. So from an experience standpoint, Jalen Brunson. Then you would go Donovan Mitchell. That third is probably in my opinion Karl-Anthony Towns. And then after that, it has been a game-by-game basis. If OG Anunoby was healthy, you would probably put him in that spot. But Mikal Bridges played well, but you look at Evan Mobley, you look at Jarrett Allen, they've had moments up and down in the postseason. If Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby outperform Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley, that's the end of the series.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye questions Cavs' defense against Knicks' offensive firepower
quotes.excerpt: I just don't think they don't really have like Dean Wade can work on when one guy is centered on the offense, but the Knicks have five playmakers.
quotes.quote: I think Jalen Brunson is going to give them the business. I just don't think they don't really have like Dean Wade can work on when one guy is centered on the offense, but the Knicks have five playmakers. If you look at Toronto, their offense was solid but not great. Detroit, their offense was great at times. But then you look at the Knicks offense is immaculate. And so what do you do if Jalen Brunson's going off? Oh, we have to double team him? Now you're leaving KAT, OG, Josh Hart, Mikal Bridges, whoever else open. It's like to me, I don't know if the Cavs' defense is up to this challenge. I'd have to see it after a game or two.

quotes.speaker: Channing Frye
quotes.summary_phrase: Channing Frye predicts Knicks in 6, Karl-Anthony Towns as ECF MVP
quotes.excerpt: I'm going out. I'm going to say Karl-Anthony Towns. I think he's going to cook this series.
quotes.quote: I got the Knicks in six. And then I have, I'm going to say, dude, I'm going out. I'm going to say Karl-Anthony Towns. I think he's going to cook this series. The Knicks can't win with a small point guard? They can't win a Finals, Finals, Finals. They get there, they get to the Finals, they ain't going to win the Finals. Because listen, I'll tell you this, the West ain't the East now. You can do what you want.

quotes.speaker: Richard Jefferson
quotes.summary_phrase: Richard Jefferson predicts Knicks in 7, Jalen Brunson as ECF MVP
quotes.excerpt: I think the Knicks have had a better season, they're playing better, consistent basketball right now.
quotes.quote: No, it's not, it's not for me to pick. No, it's not even that. I just, I think the Knicks, the Knicks have had a better season, they're playing better, consistent basketball right now. And they have the home court advantage, right? So, and if you look at how the Cavs, like this is new territory. This is a new moment. So that's where I just think Knicks in seven. Brunson.
